AfterDamageGiven.issue: Closed 2026-07-31 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 26.) The substitution is UNDONE. `on_damage_dealt`'s dispatch condition dropped `hp_lost > 0` (keeping `dealer is not None`), so the sim's dealer-side event now sees every hit including fully-blocked and zero-damage ones, matching CreatureCmd.cs:388-395 where AfterDamageGiven fires unconditionally while only AfterDamageReceived carries the killing-blow guard; a `was_fully_blocked` value was added mirroring CreatureCmd.cs's formula exactly (`not Unblockable and (absorbed > 0 or target.block > 0) and int(unblocked) == 0`, reading `absorbed` pre-modifier and `target.block` post-absorption in C#'s own order), which required hoisting `absorbed = 0` out of the has-block branch. ImbalancedPower and PaperCutsPower now listen on `on_damage_dealt` instead of filtering `on_damage_received` by dealer. Imbalanced also LOST two guards C# never had -- ImbalancedPower.cs:19 is exactly `if (dealer == base.Owner && result.WasFullyBlocked)` with no target check and no MOVE-only gate (C# gets self-exclusion for free from being dealer-side). That removal is inert on today's content: Imbalanced is applied only to BowlbugRock, whose sole move always targets the player, so the old `target is not self.owner` guard was dead code. PaperCuts' own guards were already faithful and only its hook site moved. T2's dealer-before-victim ordering and killing-blow snapshot are untouched. Pins: test/test_combat_veto_and_dealer_event.py.  The text it replaced read: WRONG HOOK. C#'s `AfterDamageGiven(choiceContext, dealer, result, props, target, cardSource)` is the DEALER-side after-damage event; the sim's counterpart is `on_damage_dealt` (hooks.py:469, fired at cmds.py:123-124), and this power uses `on_damage_received` instead, filtering on `dealer is self.owner`. The reason the port had to do that is itself the finding: cmds.py:123 fires on_damage_dealt only `if dealer is not None and hp_lost > 0`, so the sim's dealer-side event **cannot see a fully-blocked or zero-damage hit at all**, where C#'s AfterDamageGiven sees every one (`result.WasFullyBlocked` is a field it is expected to read). Consequence of the substitution: cmds.py:121's killing-blow guard suppresses the sim's on_damage_received when the hit killed the VICTIM, and cmds.py:119-120's own comment says "AfterDamageGiven (on_damage_dealt) is not guarded and still fires on the kill" -- so this power silently stops working on a lethal hit in the sim and keeps working in the game. Third-file citations, not hashed here. This unit is the sharpest instance of that shape, because the whole power keys on `result.WasFullyBlocked` (ImbalancedPower.cs:19) -- exactly the case cmds.py:123's `hp_lost > 0` makes invisible to the sim's dealer-side event. The port therefore reads `amount == 0` on the victim's hook (powers.py:2064), which is a BROADER predicate than WasFullyBlocked: hp_lost is 0 for a fully blocked hit, but also for a hit that was 0 to begin with and for one an HP-loss modifier zeroed, neither of which C# calls fully blocked. The sim then narrows it back with an added `ValueProp.MOVE in props` test (powers.py:2065) that C# does NOT have -- recurring gap shape 8 -- so the two predicates differ in both directions. DORMANT: the owner is the Bowlbug Rock (monsters/hive/bowlbugs.py:42-47), whose only damage source is its own HEADBUTT AttackIntent (props MOVE, non-zero), and the player has no ported HP-loss modifier that could zero an enemy's hit -- so the only reachable trigger is a genuine full block, where both predicates agree. Trigger: a 0-damage MOVE from the owner, or any unpowered damage the owner deals. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: powers.py:2067-2071 reproduces both arms with `hasattr(self.owner, "is_off_balance")`, and the sim's docstring says why ("BowlbugRock's move machine reads it"). Faithful, and a good example of a hasattr probe standing in for a C# type test without changing the outcome.
